acceptance: Under pytest, no test can read the real `~/.benchbox` credentials. A test proves this by seeding a sentinel credential in a fake real-home location and asserting it never appears in a built config.
Any API that returns a config containing secrets returns them masked in its repr, str and log output. A test covers this.
The guard also covers isolation with marker selection, such as `-m` live-only expressions, the case #2970 handled for logging.
Under pytest, no test writes to the real `~/.benchbox` (for example `last_run.yaml`); a test seeds a sentinel file there and asserts it is unchanged after a CLI run
context:
Reported in the general follow-ups takeover on 2026-10-15. The user was told they may want to rotate that Snowflake credential.

Related: #2970 added session isolation of HOME and logging for tests, but this path either escapes it or is reached outside pytest. The credential-profile fail-closed check from #2985 lives in `build_platform_config`. Check where the credentials manager resolves its directory, whether the session-isolation fixture redirects it, and whether any test that currently passes reads the real `~/.benchbox`.

2026-10-16: during a `make test-pytest -n 8` run, `~/.benchbox/last_run.yaml` changed while a DuckDB TPC-H generate,load test ran. Some test path may still write to the real preferences directory (`benchbox/cli/preferences.py`, around line 43). Not confirmed.
description: A worker called `PlatformHookRegistry.build_database_config("snowflake", ...)` in a local probe. The returned config contained the real Snowflake credential set from `~/.benchbox`, and the worker printed it to its terminal. Nothing reached the repository or a PR. The takeover handoff also says that this API loads real saved credentials into the returned config during tests. Tests and probes that build a config can therefore read, and may log or write, real user secrets.
